compiled_state.description:
## Problem

In `_apply_delta` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/delta_tree.py`), two git subprocesses run back to back
against the same temp index. One is bounded, the other is not:

```python
read = git_run(repo_root, "read-tree", "--end-of-options", sha, env=env)   # bounded
...
proc = run_git(
    repo_root, "checkout-index", "--force", "-z", "--stdin",
    f"--prefix={dest_tree}{os.sep}",
    check=False, env=env, input_data=payload,                              # NO timeout=
)
```

`git_run` (`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:131`) applies `timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT` (300s) and converts a
timeout into a structured failure. The `checkout-index` call bypasses that wrapper and passes no
`timeout=`, so it can block indefinitely.

## Why it matters

The unbounded call is **the expensive one**. `read-tree` populates an index; `checkout-index`
writes the actual blob content — the operation this subsystem exists to make cheaper, and the
one measured at roughly 620 MiB / 70k blobs for a full ticket tree. It is also the call that
touches the filesystem hardest, so it is the likeliest of the two to stall on a slow or wedged
volume.

A stall here has no upper bound and no diagnostic: the caller cannot distinguish "still writing"
from "hung", which is the same shape as a check that is silent when it should fire.

## Why this is a defect rather than a design choice

The asymmetry is **within a single function**, against the same index, in the same failure
domain. Nothing in the module states an intent to leave this call unbounded, and its sibling two
statements earlier is bounded. Either both should be bounded or the divergence should be stated;
today it is neither.

## Scope

Narrow: give the `checkout-index` call the same bound its sibling already has, and make a
timeout a structured failure rather than an exception escaping `_apply_delta` — the function
returns `bool` and its callers fall back to full materialization on `False`, so a timeout should
take that path.

Explicitly OUT of scope: changing `_GIT_TIMEOUT`'s value, changing `git_run`, or reworking the
delta/donor design. If 300s proves wrong for a blob-write of this size, that is a separate
calibration question — record it, do not retune it here.

## Provenance

Surfaced as a non-blocking advisory on Gerrit 1980 patchset 2 (ticket
`8386-a512-4815-4e6b`, smart-disloyal-naga) and deliberately not fixed there: it is
pre-existing in `delta_tree.py` rather than introduced by that change, and chasing it would have
widened a change already at 376 non-test lines. Verified independently against `origin/main`
before filing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `checkout-index` call in `_apply_delta` is bounded by the same timeout its sibling
      `read-tree` call uses — verified by a test that stubs the call to exceed the bound and
      asserts it is cut off rather than running unbounded
- [ ] A timeout returns `False` from `_apply_delta` (so callers fall back to full
      materialization) rather than raising out of it — verified by a test asserting the return
      value and that the caller's fallback path runs
- [ ] The timeout is surfaced in a diagnostic that names the operation, so a stall is
      distinguishable from slow progress — verified by a test asserting on the message
- [ ] `_GIT_TIMEOUT` itself is unchanged — verified by a test pinning its value
compiled_state.title: checkout-index in _apply_delta runs unbounded while its sibling read-tree is timeout-bounded
